content:
Facts: Five children sued two sisters for reduction of mother's donations (rural building halves and land to each sister, plus land to father later donated by him to same daughters) and testamentary dispositions (land to four plaintiffs and one brother); mother's will required plaintiffs to create independent access road from different route as they lacked servitude rights over donated parcels; estate included mother's one-third share of predeceased father's inheritance which she never accepted; defendants challenged special power of attorney validity and claimed incompatibility between division and reduction actions.
Legal Framework: Articles 553-564 Italian Civil Code (reduction action); Arts. 756-768 (estate division); Art. 470 (acceptance of inheritance due to deceased); Arts. 83, 125, 182 Italian Code of Civil Procedure (representation; procedural regularization); case law on action compatibility (Cass. 2367/1970, 1443/1962, 9192/2017).
Interpretive Issues: Whether defective special power of attorney cured by subsequent ratification and principal's appearance in proceedings; compatibility and cumulative admissibility of reduction action with division claim when testamentary dispositions exhaust entire estate; inclusion in hereditary mass of inheritance share never accepted by deceased; methodology for calculating legitimate portions when donations made both directly to children and indirectly through predeceased spouse's subsequent donations; treatment of testamentary burden requiring heirs to construct access infrastructure.
Principles Applied: Falsus procurator defects remedied retroactively by principal's appearance and ratification at any procedural stage; ratification validates all prior procedural acts. Retroactive regularization permitted for ineffective but not formally invalid representation acts; substantive limitation periods unaffected per Art. 182. Reduction and division claims cumulatively admissible for procedural economy when former condition precedent to latter; reduction necessary to reconstitute joint inheritance when testamentary dispositions exhaust estate. Deceased heir's unaccepted inheritance share falls to their heirs who may accept per Art. 470. Donations to spouse subsequently donated to same beneficiaries computed in available portion calculation; indirect donations through intermediary aggregated with direct donations for reduction analysis. Legitimate portion calculated as reserved two-thirds divided equally among all children; available portion limited to one-third. Testamentary burdens (infrastructure construction costs) allocated proportionally among beneficiaries based on access benefit ratio. Monetary adjustments for reduction constitute value debts requiring: revaluation per ISTAT indices, legal interest from succession opening until payment, continued revaluation until judgment publication. Division in kind impractical when donated assets indivisible; cash adjustments restore legitimate portions. Court-appointed expert determines asset values, calculates infringement amounts, and structures adjustment payments. Estate-related litigation costs (including expert fees) charged to estate; legal representation costs compensated inter partes absent fault.
